title: Built a daily swing-trading research dashboard (regime filter + setup logger). Looking for 5–10 beta testers to stress-test it live.
author: tonylul69

comments.author: timmyboy290
comments.body: Regime filters sound good on paper but fall apart fast in choppy markets.

replies.author: tonylul69
replies.body: Here's what I actually have on this, for what it's worth: I ran the regime-filtered breakout config through an 8-year backtest with out-of-sample holdout validation (tuned on one chunk of history, tested against a later chunk it never saw), +212% from tuning to holdout, on 731 out-of-sample trades, and it held up well on average (avg expectancy went *up* from tuning to holdout, not down, which is the opposite of what you'd expect from an overfit result).

comments.author: Vegetable-Rub-8241
comments.body:
Backtest block reconciles, which is rare. 1.51 PF at 69.6% means most of those wins are small exits, not the 6.0 ADR target. Fine, just worth saying out loud.

But 89.4% across 47 positions held 0 to 3 days is an unrealized mark, not a win rate. Nothing has hit a stop or a target yet, and your own out of sample pullback number is 28.1%. Leading with it makes live look three times better than your own backtest says it should be.

Also worth sitting with: a holdout is only out of sample the first time you look at it.

Disclosure, I build in this space. Separate scoring step grades a strategy on data it never saw. Not after your testers.

Blunt answer welcome: how many times had you looked at that holdout before the run you published?

replies.author: tonylul69
replies.body: to answer directly - honestly more than i should have. probably 8-10+ separate looks at holdout results across different watchlists/periods/hypotheses before landing on the numbers i posted
